starting_evidence_verified_2026_11_23: Frozen E5 (experiments/frozen/e5, verdict visual_improves_evidence): on 101 held-out evidence questions in 14 documents, the pages supplied after the context guard hold an evidence page for 66/101 under OCR + BM25 and 86/101 under ColQwen2; mean evidence recall 0.526 -> 0.721, delta +0.195 [+0.110, +0.309] (document-cluster bootstrap), sign-flip p 0.0005.

Frozen E4 (experiments/frozen/e4): the same reader answers 17/37 development questions even when given exactly the annotated evidence pages, and the shipped application 11/40. More evidence is necessary for better answers, not sufficient.

E5's pre-registered recommendation: a controlled end-to-end answering experiment, same GPT-4o-mini request format, same 768-px images and guard, A versus V pages, paid, separate spec; no integration before it.
why_this_experiment.what_e6_decides: Which retriever the application ships as its default in the application-building phase that follows E6. Both 'visual retrieval does not help' and 'cannot tell' lead to the same action (keep OCR + BM25), so the confirmatory question is one-directional: is V better than A by a meaningful margin?
why_this_experiment.what_e6_is_not: Not an integration of ColQwen2 into src/visualdoc/ and not a run of the visual model: V's pages are E5's frozen rankings, re-derived offline from E5's cached embeddings. Not a retriever comparison beyond A and V (no fusion arm, no other model, no tuning). Not a measurement of the application's indexing latency on new documents (taken from E5).

hypotheses.primary_null: On the 102 held-out answerable questions, mean over questions of (correct_V - correct_A) <= 0.
hypotheses.primary_directional: mean(correct_V - correct_A) > 0 (direction fixed by E5's evidence result before any E6 reply).
hypotheses.why_0_05: About 5 of 102 answerable questions. It equals the threshold of E4 and E5. Below it, switching the application's default retriever to a 4.4 GB model that needs about 12.5 s per page to index on the development machine (E5) is not worth its cost. A judgement fixed before any reply, not a statistical quantity.
hypotheses.pre_run_expectation: Planning only (notebook 05 section 5, planning_simulation below): if E5's evidence gain turns into answers at E4's reader rates (10/20 correct with all evidence supplied, 1/11 with none), the true difference is about +0.08 and the rule adopts V in 32-47 % of simulated experiments, ending inconclusive otherwise; at twice that effect (+0.15) it adopts V in 94-98 %; with no effect it adopts V in 1.2-2.5 %. An inconclusive result is therefore likely even if visual retrieval helps as E5 suggests.

reader.identity: the application's reader as frozen in E4 (src/visualdoc/answering.py at the module hashes pinned in experiments/specs/e4_application_end_to_end_v1.json): rebuilt visibly in notebook 05, which does not import src/visualdoc (AGENTS.md). Equivalence is checked offline: the notebook's builder reproduces the fingerprint, expected prompt tokens and prompt-token bound of all 96 frozen E4 requests, its guard reproduces E4's 57 supplied page lists, and its parser reproduces the application's parsed answer, cited pages and error on all 96 frozen E4 replies
reader.user_content: 'Question: {q}\n\nPage images:' then, for each supplied page in rank order, the text '[Page N]' and the page's 768-px PNG as a base64 data URL with detail high
reader.image: whole page fitted in a 768 x 1536-px box, opaque RGB PNG (E1 profile); held-out images are E5's renders, verified by SHA-256 against experiments/frozen/e5/tables/render_manifest_heldout.csv
reader.context_guard: keep the longest ranked prefix of the top 5 such that 100 framing tokens + UTF-8 bytes of the system prompt + UTF-8 bytes of the question header + sum over kept pages of (UTF-8 bytes of '[Page N]' + billed image tokens) <= 128,000 - 400; never reorders
reader.image_tokens: GPT-4o-mini high detail: fit in 2048 x 2048, reduce the short side to 768 if larger, 2,833 + 5,667 per 512-px tile
reader.pre_call_check: known model, positive bounded output, prompt-token bound + 400 <= 128,000, cost bound <= USD 0.02 per request; a failing request raises before any call
reader.parser: strict JSON: 'answer' required; 'cited_pages' a list of whole page numbers >= 1 (an integer, a whole float such as 2.0, or ASCII digits); anything else makes the reply unparseable; 'not answerable' in any case normalised to 'Not answerable'; a reply whose finish_reason is not 'stop' is an error
reader.citations: valid = every cited page was supplied; off_by_one = every invalid page equals a supplied page minus 1; missing = an answer other than 'Not answerable' with no citation; cites_evidence = at least one cited page is an annotated evidence page (evaluation only)

design.type: one session; two arms of the same reader that differ only in the list of pages supplied; every question sent once per arm as an adjacent, counterbalanced pair

A.label: application retriever: OCR + BM25
A.pages: E5 arm A's full ranking (frozen rankings.parquet), top 5, then the context guard

V.label: visual retriever: ColQwen2 v1.0
V.pages: E5 arm V's full ranking (frozen rankings.parquet; vidore/colqwen2-v1.0-hf @ ddc07d23, MaxSim over every page), top 5, then the same context guard

control_by_construction: A and V share the system prompt, question header, page-tag format, 768-px images, model snapshot, parameters, guard, parser and scorer; only which pages are supplied, how many, and in which order differs
the guard keeps 4 pages for 105 questions and 3 for 13 questions in both arms, so request length is matched
no A request equals its V request (0 of 118 byte-identical; 6 supply the same page set in a different order)

reuse_of_e5.questions: E5's held-out set: every question about the 14 documents E5 selected (selection rule and list in experiments/specs/e5_visual_retrieval_v1.json)
reuse_of_e5.rankings: experiments/frozen/e5/tables/rankings.parquet, held-out rows of arms A and V; the copy is verified against experiments/frozen/e5/SHA256SUMS
reuse_of_e5.verification_of_A: BM25 rebuilt in notebook 05 from E5's held-out page text (data/processed/mmlongbench_doc/e5/heldout_pages.parquet) gives the identical full ranking for all 118 questions
reuse_of_e5.verification_of_V: MaxSim recomputed in NumPy from E5's cached bf16 embeddings (data/cache/e5/colqwen2-v1.0-hf@ddc07d2317c8/<config hash>/) gives the identical full ranking for all 118 questions; no model is loaded and nothing is encoded
reuse_of_e5.supplied_pages: the pages each arm supplies after the guard equal E5's frozen supplied_A and supplied_V on the 101 evidence questions

design.why_no_variability_margin: E4 needed a cross-session margin because its control was a frozen run from another day. Here both arms run in the same session, interleaved as adjacent pairs with balanced order, so drift and cross-day changes affect both arms alike; the reader's per-request randomness is part of each observed difference and therefore of the document bootstrap and the sign-flip test. A second replicate of both arms (about USD 3.7) does not fit the USD 5.60 ceiling.
design.no_pilot: The request format is E4's (98 calls without a format failure). E6's largest request is no larger than E4's largest (checked offline), and the smoke pair tests it.

reconciliation_101_vs_102.effect_bound: it can move the primary difference by at most 1/102 = 0.0098; the sensitivity analysis on the 101 evidence questions reports the result without it

roles.primary: the 102 answerable questions (accuracy does not need evidence annotations, so mmlb-0599 is included)
roles.all_questions: 118, for the benchmark's overall accuracy and F1 and for citation validity

population.questions_per_document: 4 to 16 (AMAZON_2017_10K 15, COSTCO_2021_10K 16); the two 10-K filings hold 31 of 102 answerable questions

strata_preregistered.definition: computed from the annotated evidence pages E and each arm's supplied pages S before any E6 reply; per arm: all (E subset of S), some (E and S intersect, E not a subset of S), none (E and S disjoint); descriptive, never part of the verdict
strata_preregistered.use: the decomposition of the primary difference by group shows whether any accuracy change sits where V changed the evidence (the mechanism E5 measured) or where it did not (distractor pages, page order)

scoring.scorer: the frozen MMLongBench-Doc rule-based scorer of notebook 03 section 1, rebuilt visibly in notebook 05 and checked on its 17 hand-traced cases and by re-scoring every frozen E4 reply to the frozen E4 scores
scoring.correct: score > 0 (the project's definition since E1; ANLS partial credit above 0.5 counts)
scoring.unanswerable: correct when the parsed answer is exactly 'Not answerable'
scoring.S1_reference_unscorable: held-out questions whose reference answer scores below 1 against itself; computed offline before any reply and listed in sensitivity.S1_qids

primary.name: answer accuracy on the 102 held-out answerable questions
primary.estimand: Delta = (1/102) * sum over questions of (correct_V - correct_A), question-weighted
primary.reported_with: A and V accuracy, fixed (A wrong, V right), broken (A right, V wrong), both correct, both wrong

citation_correctness: citation validity on all 118 replies per arm: every cited page supplied and no answer without a citation
grounded citation on the 101 evidence questions: an answer (not 'Not answerable') whose citations are valid, non-empty and include at least one annotated evidence page
correct and grounded on the 101 evidence questions
off-by-one printed page numbers among invalid citations; answers without a citation
abstention: correct abstention on the 16 unanswerable questions
false abstention on the 102 answerable questions, split by whether the arm supplied an evidence page (abstaining when none was supplied is grounded behaviour, reported as such although it scores 0)
unsupported answers: an answer when no evidence page was supplied (answerable) or on an unanswerable question
latency: API latency per call (median and 90th percentile) per arm, measured in the same session

retrieval latency per question from E5's frozen measurements on the development machine: BM25 query 0.13 ms vs ColQwen2 query encoding 0.16 s + MaxSim 4.4 ms; indexing per page: BM25 0.08 ms (+0.10 s text extraction incl. OCR) vs ColQwen2 12.5 s
end-to-end latency per question excluding indexing = retrieval + API, per arm
efficiency_beside_answer_quality: reported in the same evaluation output as the primary result, per arm and per held-out document, from E5's frozen measurements on the development machine (fanless Apple M1, MPS, bf16): measured ColQwen2 indexing seconds per page image (vision + language pass) and per document, embedding storage per page and per document (cached bf16 safetensors), model weights 4.42 GB, peak GPU memory about 3.3 GB, query encoding about 0.16 s; against BM25: index about 0.1 ms per page and text extraction (with OCR where needed) about 0.1 s per page, no model
descriptive only: efficiency never changes the verdict, but the deployment action for adopt_visual_retrieval must state how indexing time and storage are handled
cost: billed prompt, completion and cached prompt tokens per arm
list-price USD per question and in total per arm; V / A cost ratio
ColQwen2's local resources from E5: 4.42 GB weights, 193 KB of embeddings per page, about 3.3 GB peak GPU memory

sensitivity.rule: reported beside the primary; never change the verdict
analyses: document-weighted mean difference (each document weighs 1/14) with its own sign-flip test

metrics.mechanism_descriptive: Delta, fixed and broken within the three stratum groups above; per document

statistics.unit: question, paired across arms; questions cluster within 14 documents (4-16 questions each), so every interval and test resamples or permutes whole documents
statistics.interval: document-cluster percentile bootstrap: draw 14 documents with replacement, Delta* = (sum of the drawn documents' summed differences) / (sum of their question counts); 10,000 resamples from numpy.random.default_rng(20261127) as one integers(0, 14, size=(10000, 14)) call over documents sorted by name; reported: one-sided 95 % lower bound (5th percentile) for the decision and the two-sided 95 % interval (2.5th, 97.5th)
statistics.test: exact document-level sign-flip permutation test of T = sum over documents of D_d, D_d = sum over the document's questions of (correct_V - correct_A); under H0 the arm labels are exchangeable within each document, so each of the 2^14 = 16,384 sign vectors is equally likely; one-sided p = share of sign vectors with T* >= T_observed (primary), two-sided p = share with |T*| >= |T_observed| (reported)
statistics.why_these: Both respect the clustering and match the question-weighted estimand. The bootstrap with 14 clusters can under-cover; the exact permutation test needs no large-sample approximation, and the rule requires both. The same implementation reproduces E5's frozen interval and p-value exactly on E5's data (checked offline).
descriptive_only: exact McNemar test on fixed and broken (ignores clustering)
statistics.multiplicity: one primary endpoint and one test decide; every secondary and sensitivity result is descriptive

decision_rule.applies_to: the primary endpoint of the main replicate of a complete, validated full run

guardrails.G1: correct abstentions on the 16 unanswerable questions: V >= A - 2
guardrails.G2: citation validity on the 118 replies: V - A >= -0.05

outcomes.adopt_visual_retrieval: C1, C2, C3 and C4 hold, and G1 and G2 hold
outcomes.visual_gain_with_regression: C1-C4 hold but G1 or G2 fails
outcomes.visual_worse: Delta <= -0.05 and the two-sided 95 % bootstrap upper bound < 0
outcomes.no_meaningful_difference: the two-sided 95 % bootstrap interval lies inside (-0.05, +0.05)

statistical_reading.adopt_visual_retrieval: Evidence, at one-sided alpha 0.05 with documents as the unit of inference, that V answers more held-out questions correctly than A, by an estimated margin of at least 0.05; guardrails met. A claim about this population of questions and documents, not about every document type.
statistical_reading.visual_gain_with_regression: The same accuracy evidence, but a pre-registered safety guardrail failed.
statistical_reading.visual_worse: Evidence that V answers meaningfully fewer questions correctly (estimate <= -0.05, two-sided 95 % upper bound < 0).
statistical_reading.no_meaningful_difference: The two-sided 95 % interval excludes differences of 0.05 or more in either direction: any difference is smaller than the meaningful margin.
statistical_reading.inconclusive: The data neither establish a meaningful gain nor exclude one. This is not evidence that ColQwen2 is ineffective; the point estimate and interval are reported as they are.

decision_rule.evidence_versus_deployment: The verdict is a statistical reading of E6; the recommendation is a deployment decision. For every verdict except adopt_visual_retrieval the deployment action is the same: keep OCR + BM25 as the application's default, because it is the status quo, needs no model and indexes in milliseconds. Keeping BM25 after an inconclusive result is a product default under uncertainty, not a finding that visual retrieval does not help; E5's evidence-level result stands.

recommendation_map.adopt_visual_retrieval: Make ColQwen2 the application's default retriever in the application-building phase (a change to src/visualdoc that needs the owner's separate approval, per AGENTS.md), keeping OCR + BM25 as the fallback where the model cannot run. The integration must index pages once at upload (about 12.5 s per page on the development machine) and cache the embeddings.
recommendation_map.visual_gain_with_regression: Keep OCR + BM25 as the default; the owner decides on the reported trade-off before any integration.
recommendation_map.visual_worse: Keep OCR + BM25; reject visual retrieval for this application.
recommendation_map.no_meaningful_difference: Keep OCR + BM25: the gain does not justify the model and the indexing cost.
recommendation_map.inconclusive: Keep OCR + BM25 as the default and build the application; report the interval and state that ColQwen2's benefit is unresolved, not refuted. No further retrieval experiment is planned before the application exists.

never_change_the_verdict: secondary metrics other than G1 and G2
decision_rule.fixed_before_results: the rule, its thresholds, the metrics, the strata, the sensitivity sets, seeds and the simulation are frozen in this spec before any E6 reply; a change requires a new spec version, and the v1 result under the v1 rule is still reported

planning_simulation.status: planning only, computed in notebook 05 section 5 before any reply; never a result and never part of the decision
planning_simulation.assumptions: per question, the probability of a correct answer depends only on the evidence its arm supplies (all / some / none), at rates from frozen E4's application replies: all 10/20 = 0.5, none 1/11; some = none or = all (two scenarios), or the all-none gap doubled; mmlb-0599 counts as none in both arms; the two arms of a question share their latent uniform draw with probability rho (0.73 makes identical-input arms at p = 0.5 disagree at E4's cross-session rate of 5/37; 0.5 is a less dependent case); guardrails assumed met
planning_simulation.method: 2,000 simulated experiments per row on the 102 answerable questions and their real documents, each analysed with the frozen functions (2,000 bootstrap draws instead of 10,000 for speed; exact sign-flip test); seed 20261128

budget.scope: cumulative over every E6 run under this spec version (smoke, full, retries, and any interrupted or resumed run), at list price
budget.enforcement: before each call: list-price cost of every reply already received by any E6 run under this spec hash, plus the full upper bound of every attempt that failed after it may have been processed (network, server or unexpected error; never a 4xx), plus the upper bound of this and every remaining call of the current run, must stay within the ceiling. The per-call upper bound is the prompt-token bound, uncached, plus the full 400-token output allowance

estimate_typical_usd.note: exact expected prompt tokens, the mean E4 reply length (21.7 output tokens), no cache discount

budget.headroom: 5.60 - 3.8003 = 1.7997 USD (48 % of a full run) for retries, possibly billed failed attempts and a resumed run
budget.price_basis: OpenAI list price, USD 0.15 / 0.60 per 1M input / output tokens; cached input is billed lower, so the bound is conservative

limitations: 102 answerable questions in 14 documents: at the effect E5's evidence gain implies (about +0.08) the rule adopts V in only 32-47 % of simulated experiments; 'inconclusive' is a likely outcome and means 'not shown', not 'no effect'.
One replicate: per-request reader randomness is inside the observed differences but not separately measured.
The primary difference mixes evidence availability with distractor pages and page order; the strata separate the first only.
Possible overlap between ColQwen2's training data and held-out documents (would favour V); documents of at most 100 pages.
Single annotations: an answer on an unannotated page counts as unsupported by evidence in the strata, though it can still be scored correct.
Latency of visual indexing is taken from E5 on one fanless M1, not measured in an application.
The model snapshot shuts down on 2027-01-14.
